name: Boxer Step
description: Weight rocks from foot to foot like a boxer shadowboxing, instead of landing on both feet together. One foot taps down lightly while the other carries most of the weight, and they swap every rope pass.
tips: Stay on the balls of your feet the whole time — flat heels will slow the rhythm down.
Start slower than feels natural; the weight shift only needs to be a few centimeters.

videos.title: Learn The Jump Rope Boxer Skip In 5 Easy Steps

name: Crossover
description: Your hands cross in front of your body right before the rope passes under your feet, so the loop comes down crossed instead of open — the entry point for every criss-cross style trick.
tips: Cross at the wrists, not the elbows, and keep your hands close together so the loop stays small.
Jump through the crossed loop before you worry about uncrossing — the exit can wait until the cross feels automatic.

name: Criss-Cross
description: The full open-cross-open cycle: jump through the rope normally, cross your arms for one pass, then uncross and return to open hands — repeated as a steady rhythm instead of a one-off crossover.
tips: Think 'open, cross, open, cross' out loud at first to keep the pattern even.
Keep your arms low and close to your hips — reaching wide to cross makes the rope catch your feet.

videos.title: Learn The Jump Rope Criss Cross

name: 360° Turn
description: You spin your whole body a full circle over several ordinary jumps while the rope keeps turning underneath at the normal one-pass rhythm — the rope doesn't change, your orientation does.
tips: Spot a point on the wall and spin toward it in small stages across 3-4 jumps rather than one big twist.
Keep your wrists steady through the turn; let your whole arm rotate with your body instead of fighting it.
